observations: Photo 0: A disassembled engine block sitting on a brick/paver surface, with people and furniture in the background suggesting a roadside or yard workshop, not a professional garage.
Photo 0 and 1: Valve covers clearly embossed with the word 'PORSCHE' in raised lettering.
Photo 1: Visible oily/greasy residue and discoloration around the valve cover and exhaust manifold area, suggesting a possible oil leak or seep.
Photo 2: Another angle of the same engine, showing wiring harness connectors, intake manifold, and a loose tire/cart in the background, confirming an informal outdoor setting.
No VIN plate, engine code sticker, dipstick, oil fill cap close-up, or serial number visible in any photo.
No video, startup clip, or compression test shown to support 'tested and working' or 'no knock' claims.
No odometer, paperwork, or import documentation visible to support 'low mileage' or 'direct from Belgium' claims.
Watermark 'EZE PORSCHE GLOBAL AUTOS' overlaid on all three photos, which is the seller's own branding, not independent proof.
Seller's new message is a verbal reassurance only; no new photo, video, or document was provided.

identity.kind: complete used car engine, pulled/removed unit (Porsche branded valve covers, exact model/engine code not legible)

claims.evidence: No shipping documents, customs paperwork, or Belgian markings visible in any photo; seller's reassurance adds no visual proof.
Seller now says 'I tested it myself yesterday' but this is a verbal claim with no video, sound, or diagnostic readout; engine remains shown static and partially disassembled.
Requires audio/video of a running engine, which is still not provided.
No odometer, mileage sticker, or service history visible in any photo.

risks.risk: Engine could be non-functional or have internal damage (knock, worn bearings, cracked block) since it is shown static and disassembled
risks.proof: A clear video of the engine running/idling with audible sound, plus a compression test printout
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / non-running core engine

risks.risk: Oily residue near valve cover/exhaust area in photo 1 may indicate an oil leak or gasket failure
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the valve cover gasket and oil pan seams after wiping clean, or a pressure test
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming leak present, needing gasket work

risks.risk: Exact engine model/code cannot be read, so correct fitment and comparable market value cannot be confirmed
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine code/serial plate, usually stamped on the block near the bellhousing
risks.if_unproven: priced at generic used-Porsche-engine floor, not model-specific premium

risks.risk: Completeness of accessories (turbo/supercharger if applicable, sensors, wiring harness, ECU) cannot be confirmed; missing parts reduce value substantially
risks.proof: Full 360-degree photo set showing intake, exhaust manifolds, turbo housing (if any), and harness connectors intact

risks.risk: 'Tokunbo' (fairly used/import) origin and low mileage claims cannot be confirmed, affecting resale and remaining lifespan value
risks.proof: Import documents, Belgian de-registration papers, or mileage certificate
risks.if_unproven: priced as unknown-mileage used engine, not low-mileage premium

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the engine code/serial number stamp on the block
Video of the engine running with audible sound (to support 'tested, working, no knock')
Close-up of valve cover gaskets and oil pan for leak assessment
Photos showing all sides of the engine including turbo/supercharger unit if equipped, and full wiring harness
Any import/customs paperwork showing Belgian origin and mileage
response.reason: A verbal reassurance without any new photo or video does not change the evidentiary basis; all performance and provenance claims remain unverifiable_remote, so the engine is still priced at worst-case (non-verified, non-running, generic) pending actual proof.
